data.hypothesis: A scalar two-group unroll can expose independent table lookups to the processor and halve loop-control frequency relative to a single eight-character group. Requiring 20 remaining characters reads only the two complete groups while leaving a quartet for scalar padding/tail handling. There are no candidate timings yet; the baseline is correct at about 55.0 µs mean, and h01's two-group attempt failed to build because line separators were emitted as literal escape sequences.
data.notes: This is a bounded scalar scheduling test: lookup loads are interleaved across two eight-character groups, output is written as exact six-byte results, and the final quartet is decoded without overread. No explicit SIMD or parallel execution is added; the threads argument is unused. The earlier h01 attempt did not produce correctness or timing results. The controller should validate empty/short inputs, group-boundary lengths, all padding cases, random valid strings, and Lena before repeated native timing; no speedup is claimed.
transformations: Interleave scalar table lookups from two independent eight-character groups and decode 16 input characters to 12 output bytes per bulk iteration.
Keep a 20-character remaining-input guard so the bulk loop reads only complete unpadded groups; decode padding and the tail quartet scalarly.
Retain scalar execution only, without explicit SIMD or parallel work.
